sys-backup (NEW SYSTEM) — a pre-merge backup so a merge can never lose the code it replaced. Built drsamonline/backup (PUBLIC: backup.py + a reusable workflow + README + 17 tests) and drsamonline/dumps (the store). It snapshots a repo's tarball at the ref about to be replaced into <owner>__<repo>/<date-time>/<repo>.tar.gz, keeps the newest 100 per repo (deleting the oldest beyond), and creates dumps-2, dumps-3 ... when a dumps repo passes its size cap, so a full repo cannot block a backup. PROVEN: the first real dump is in drsamonline/dumps (ml-kit @ fbeb57d, 8947 B, read back byte-for-byte), and 17 unit tests pass; disabling rotation fails 4. Wired into forge via .github/workflows/backup.yml (on pull_request -> snapshots the BASE commit). TWO THINGS FOR THE OWNER: (1) add the BACKUP_TOKEN secret (contents:write on dumps, contents:read on the source) - without it the job SKIPS with a warning, it does not fail the PR and does not pretend it ran; (2) drsamonline/dumps is PRIVATE on purpose, because it will hold forge's private code - making it public would publish it.

fix-kit-tests-and-lint (owner-reported: 'every kit's test is failing in run'). ROOT CAUSE 1: app-builder's 'All kit tests' failed on EVERY run, but not on the kits - discovery called `gh api user/repos`, which the repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN cannot call, so the `|| echo '[]'` swallowed the error and fromJSON('[]') made an EMPTY MATRIX, which fails the job. It now reads the public list (`users/drsamonline/repos`) and REFUSES an empty matrix with an error that says why. ROOT CAUSE 2 (found while there): forge's lint reported 13 findings, ALL of them artifacts of the linter itself - it never de-indented a run: block, so a here-document terminator looked indented (SC1039/SC1072/SC1073), and it substituted ${{ }} with the CONSTANT 'PLACEHOLDER', so `[ -n "$x" ]` read as always-true (SC2157). Fixed both (de-indent like YAML does; substitute a VARIABLE), PROVED with `bash -n` that the de-indented block is valid shell and the indented one is not, and confirmed the old linter still reports 13 while the fixed one is clean. Added a P6 owner-reported tier to BACKLOG.md with all of these.

sys-adopt-new-repos (owner: 'THE WHOLE WORKFLOW SHOULD AUTO ADD AND APPLY TO ANY NEW REPO THAT IS PUSHED WITHOUT WORKFLOW'). tools/adopt.py + .github/workflows/adopt.yml (daily): lists the repos, finds the ones MISSING a standard workflow that APPLIES, and adds it. A page gets pages.yml; a repo with a test gets test.yml. sys-self-diagnose (self-fix, part of #26). Built tools/self-diagnose.py + .github/workflows/self-diagnose.yml (daily) - the check that was MISSING: every other check looked at a repo's contents, none at the machinery doing the checking, which is why a schedule could sit dead and a workflow could reference a script that does not exist with no report saying so. FOUR CHECKS: (1) every workflow parses; (2) the cron is a real five-field schedule with a computable period; (3) IT ACTUALLY FIRES - a scheduled workflow whose last SCHEDULED run is older than twice its period is reported as not-firing, or never-fired if there is none (this is the check that would have caught the owner's 'scheduled but never ran'); (4) every local file a run: block names (a script under tools/, a test file) really exists in the repo. Read-only - it repairs nothing; self-heal.yml does the repairing. 14 self-tests run in CI first. Writes registry/diagnose.json + DIAGNOSE.md. STILL OPEN: self-update (self-heal already exists).

sys-self-update (self-fix, #26 complete). tools/self-update.py + .github/workflows/self-update.yml (weekly). The workflows pin their actions and NOTHING watched the pins - the cost was in every run's log: 'Node.js 20 is deprecated... actions/checkout@v4', a warning on every job in every repo. The tool reads every pin, asks the latest major, and reports. REAL FINDINGS on the first run: actions/checkout@v4 -> v7.0.1 and actions/setup-python@v5 -> v7.1.0, so the whole system is two majors behind. It REPORTS and does not bump: a major bump can be breaking, so a human sees the diff. 8 self-tests. #26 IS NOW COMPLETE: self-heal (existed), self-diagnose (built), self-update (built).

fix-refresh-push (found by RENDERING the console in headless Chromium and noticing the leaderboard still showed its fallback). ROOT CAUSE, from the run log: the dashboard's refresh regenerated and committed data.json correctly, then died at `git push` - 'error: failed to push some refs to https://github.com/drsamonline/dashboard'. The HEALTH workflow commits SPEC-GAP.json + runs.json to the same branch every few minutes and is fast, so the refresh (about 80 seconds) ALWAYS lost the race. That is why data.json sat at 11:00:33 while the leaderboard still carried the dict-licence error and the roadmap still showed the hard-coded list - both fixed in app-builder hours earlier. Fix: fetch, rebase onto origin/<branch>, retry the push up to 4 times; and cancel-in-progress: false so a refresh is not killed by its own next trigger. LESSON: 'the code is fixed on main' is not 'the page shows it' - the refresh had been failing for four runs and nothing surfaced it.

self-diagnose-failures. Extended tools/self-diagnose.py: it now checks whether a workflow SUCCEEDS, not only whether it fires. app-encrypted-case-log (P4, the first of the eight apps; master-list #128). Built to its spec, composing crypto-kit + case-kit + search-kit + export-kit + web-kit and re-implementing none of them. THE VAULT: a random DEK encrypts the records and the passphrase only WRAPS it (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600k, a random 16-byte salt), so changing the passphrase never re-encrypts a record; a 24-word recovery code wraps the SAME DEK; a verifier makes a wrong passphrase fail cleanly. THE RECORDS: one per blob, a FRESH 96-bit IV each time, and the record id as AAD so a record cannot be swapped or replayed. The page carries connect-src 'none' - stricter than the spec's default-src 'self' - so an outbound request is impossible. 15 SELF-TESTS, no browser needed (Node 20's WebCrypto + the app's in-memory store fallback): the vault, the AAD binding, the recovery path, a wrong passphrase failing cleanly, no IV reuse, the ciphertext never containing the plaintext, the search, case-kit's interchange, and export -> wipe -> import -> identical data. TWO REAL BUGS MY OWN TESTS CAUGHT: I called Case.exportRecord({patient, cases}) when it takes (cases, patient), and Search.query() returns an ARRAY not {results}; and the record shape had to BE case-kit's, because Case.create() keeps only its own fields and dropped my custom label.

app-delivery-pipeline (owner: 'when an app is developed its build pipeline should also activate - full app, beautified README with badges, unique landing page with download links and screenshots, live demo where applicable, app release. i see u did nothing in the above app'). TRUE, and the criticism was fair: app-encrypted-case-log had a README and a test workflow and NOTHING ELSE - no landing page, no demo, no release, no build pipeline, so nothing was downloadable and nothing was published. Built tools/app-deliver.py: from an app's OWN metadata (its <title>, its <h1>, its meta description, the kits it vendors) it generates docs/index.html (a landing page with the .exe/.apk download links, the features, the demo and the source), docs/play/ (the LIVE DEMO - the app itself plus the kits it loads), robots.txt, sitemap.xml, .github/workflows/build-apps.yml (the tiny caller into app-builder's build.yml, which builds the EXE + APK, publishes the rolling app-latest release and deploys the demo - all from ONE commit) and the README badge block. Applied to app-encrypted-case-log: 14 files committed, which also ran the pipeline for the first time. NOT per-app hard-coded - two apps get two different pages - so it is the automation the owner asked for, and it is committed to forge to be wired into adopt.

app-delivery-linux-shot (owner: 'why did the above build not go through forge workflow? or it's missing, then add the whole workflow in forge and app-builder; app-builder should build a Linux version when applicable for all app repos; wire screenshots into the READMEs'). THREE ANSWERS. (1) WHY NOT FORGE: a PUBLIC repository can only call a reusable workflow that is ALSO public, and forge is private - so the pipeline CANNOT live in forge. It lives in app-builder (public) on purpose, and its header says so. (2) WHY THE BUILD FAILED: from the run log - the EXE, the APK and the release all SUCCEEDED; only 'Deploy the demo' died with 'Get Pages site failed ... Not Found', because a BRAND-NEW repo has no Pages site. The pipeline was not wrong; the site was never switched on. Pages is now enabled, and app-deliver.py turns it on as part of delivering. (3) LINUX: build.py already produced a native POSIX binary (it picks the --add-data separator from os.name) but nothing wired it in, so Linux users had nothing to download. A linux job now builds it and SMOKE-TESTS it - starts the binary, reads the loopback URL it prints, fetches the page, checks it is HTML - because compiling is not serving; the release waits on all three builds and ships all three assets. (4) SCREENSHOTS: a real one, captured by DRIVING the app (set a passphrase, acknowledge the recovery code, add a patient, save a note) rather than a blank first screen; it is in the README between markers and on the landing page, and a new `shot` job re-captures the LIVE demo after each deploy so the picture cannot show an older build than the one you can download.

pipeline-enables-pages (owner: 'add enabling pages in the workflow too so the pipeline works properly'). Right: I had enabled Pages by HAND for one app, which does not scale and is exactly the kind of manual step that gets forgotten. The deploy job in app-builder's build.yml now checks for a Pages site and CREATES one (build_type=workflow) when it is missing - treating 'already on' as success, and warning with the exact setting to change if the token cannot do it, instead of failing silently. So a repo the pipeline has just been given can now finish green: build the EXE, the APK and the Linux binary, publish the release, enable Pages, deploy the demo, and screenshot it.

launcher-flush. The Linux smoke test failed with 'the binary never printed a URL' and the BINARY WAS FINE: Python block-buffers stdout when it is not a terminal, so with the output redirected (`> run.log &`) the banner and the URL stayed in the buffer and never appeared. Anything supervising the binary - a smoke test, a wrapper, a log - was blind to it. The launcher now line-buffers stdout (reconfigure(line_buffering=True)), and the smoke test sets PYTHONUNBUFFERED and prints what it actually saw plus whether the process was still alive, instead of only that it saw nothing. Worth noting: the smoke test found a REAL defect in the shipped launcher on its first run - which is the argument for testing that it SERVES, not just that it compiles.

control-panel (owner: check every repo, find all the workflows, see what is connected and what is not, each function each step each stage, save it all to a new repo called control panel that controls the workflows and connects to the dashboard, then plan the best routes that cut user input to 1-2, with buttons to run each phase separately but connected as a grand pipeline from scratch to production to delivery to self-improvement and repair). BUILT. tools/fetch.py pulls every repo's workflows; tools/scan.py parses them and works out the graph; tools/plan.py derives the stages and the routes; docs/index.html is the panel. FIRST SCAN: 64 repos, 112 workflows, 134 jobs, 462 steps, 12 reusable, 24 scheduled, 96 runnable by hand, 42 connections - 0 BROKEN (no call to a workflow that does not exist), 0 PARSE ERRORS, and 8 REUSABLE WORKFLOWS NOTHING CALLS (forge's audit/docs/fanout/pages/release/self-heal/test + app-builder's test) - which is the public-caller-cannot-reach-a-private-repo constraint showing up as dead weight. THE GRAND PIPELINE: SCRATCH (3) -> BUILD (77) -> DELIVER (18) -> REPAIR (14), with every workflow placed and none unplaced. THE ROUTES: a new app = ONE input (describe it); change an app = ZERO; repair = ZERO; ship on demand = ONE press. 96 Run buttons, each linking to the real dispatch so no token lives in a browser. Verified by rendering the panel: 96 buttons, the four stages, the routes, the findings. Connected to the dashboard, which now reads the panel's plan.json live.

control-panel-gaps-routes (owner: find missing suggestive elements; how does Forge embed in this; this should go for the final commercial project; tweak, optimize, update, recreate the workflow in different simulations and choose the best routes). GAPS: 109 no-timeout, 51 no-concurrency (the exact race that broke the dashboard refresh), 31 no-permissions, 16 un-runnable, 8 orphans, 5 DRIFTED FAMILIES ('Build + deploy' x33 with a 393B spread - the file whose drift once deleted a release). control-panel-interactions (owner: what about those 8 reusable workflows, deduplication, and cross-action leading to failure). BUILT tools/interactions.py + tools/migrate.py. ORPHANS: verdicts, not labels - forge/pages.yml + forge/test.yml have public twins (a private reusable is unreachable from a public app) so they are duplicates to delete; app-builder/test.yml is public, callable, and uncalled. DEDUPE: 5 families with a canonical + a safe migration that only rewrites copies matching the caller shape. CROSS-ACTION: 3 races (forge has 11 writers), 3 permission gaps, 1 pile-up. THE REAL BUG: forge/new-app.yml granted contents:read while calling a pipeline that needs contents:write + pages:write + id-token:write, so a scaffolded app's first build would fail at run time - FIXED. AND MY OWN CHECKS WERE WRONG THREE TIMES, all corrected: drift measured in BYTES flagged 33 identical callers as drifted (it now compares STRUCTURE - the 2 odd copies carry a deliberate extra job); `gh release` is not a push, so the 6 'loops' were false (now 0); and a shared concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:false is deliberate serialisation, not a collision (3 -> 0). I also truncated tools/scan.py with a write-while-reading patch and had to restore it from the repo.

mass-sweep (owner: 'do all and updated mass sweep and panel work'). BUILT tools/sweep.py and RAN IT: 63 repos, 109 workflow files, 0 failures. The four rules - permissions, concurrency, timeout-minutes, workflow_dispatch - applied only where absent, with three safety properties: every result is parsed as YAML BEFORE writing and a rule whose result would not parse is dropped for that file; comments are preserved because the edits are line insertions, not a re-dump; and it NEVER DOWNGRADES a workflow that writes, because inferring `contents: read` for something that comments on a PR would break it - a broken workflow is worse than a broad token. THE PANEL now carries the orphan verdicts, the cross-action findings and the duplication families. Verified by reading five of the swept files back from GitHub.

queue-ideas-autobuild-killswitch (owner: there is ALREADY an app list queued on the dashboard - add app ideas to THAT queue, 133 are already queued; do not create new files when files already exist; add a scheduled workflow that checks every repo and applies what is missing; add a backlog of app ideas so they build automatically; a killswitch that stops a project midway and reverses it; and make the queued ideas build automatically if it is not already doing that). USED THE EXISTING FILES THROUGHOUT. The machinery already existed: forge/APP_MASTER_LIST.md (133 rows), forge/QUEUE/ (43 spec files), registry/plan.json + dashboard/plan.json (the machine-readable copy the console reads), new-app.yml, and scripts/new-app.py. ADDED 20 IDEAS to the EXISTING master list (133 -> 153, header count updated) and mirrored them into BOTH plan.json files: the three the QUEUE already held but the list never carried (Endpoints, Pull the Plug, Story Engine) plus 17 new ones in the categories the list already uses, every one offline, single-file and buildable from the kits that exist. Rule 0 from scripts/new-app.py still holds: an app comes from the list, by name, with a spec - so an idea without one is SKIPPED, never guessed. parity-gate (owner: honestly - do we need to retrofit old repos onto the kits? if a kit does LESS than the app, the app breaks; do not retrofit onto weaker kits; harvest the app's better code INTO the kit instead; all of this in the workflow). THE ANSWER, WITH EVIDENCE: no app is broken. Every method the three retrofitted apps call exists - export-kit exposes save, saveZip, crc32, toBytes, zip. My first two attempts to check this were WRONG and reported 18 'broken calls' that were false positives: the kits export a factory object so the methods are object-literal keys, and aethelgard-rpg-engine has its OWN object named `Game` (reported against game-kit) while lan-kit calls its own name. THE POLICY IS NOW A GATE in the existing tools/kit-audit.py, not a promise: PARITY (the kit exposes every method the app CALLS -> the app may delegate, nothing can be lost), HARVEST (the app does MORE -> the KIT gets the app's approach; the kit strengthens, the app keeps working; NEVER the reverse), BROKEN (a method that does not exist -> restore or add). The default for anything unclear is HARVEST, never retrofit. exposed_names() reads three sources, loaded_kits() only counts kits the page actually LOADS, and an unreadable kit says NOTHING rather than guessing - because a gate that cries wolf sends you to 'fix' apps that were never broken, which is what happened twice today. ALSO: run_parity() was committed before the --parity flag existed, so it was unreachable; the flag is now wired and verified.

parity-in-workflow. The parity gate now RUNS in kit-audit.yml (weekly + on demand), so the policy is enforced rather than promised: for every repo that LOADS a kit, does that kit expose every method the repo CALLS? PARITY permits a retrofit, HARVEST sends the app's better code INTO the kit, BROKEN means restore or add. It also runs on every project the owner uploads, so new code is checked against the kits and anything better is harvested into them. Verified the flag reaches the function and the normal audit still runs.
